text.p: Zimbabwe hammered England's demoralised bowlers in the third and final one-day international on Friday, reaching 249 for seven.
Captain Alistair Campbell led the spree with 80 not out, a wonderfully paced innings from 103 balls.
He featured in stands worth 74 and 50 with the Flower brothers, Grant and Andy, before staying to anchor his side through the vital late overs.
Opener Grant Flower scored 62 from 87 balls with elder brother Andy thrashing 35 from just 30 deliveries.

At the end both Dave Houghton and Paul Strang hit out valuably and England were faced with a big task if they were to finish the Zimbabwean leg of their winter tour with something at last to celebrate.
England's bowling display was a real mixed bag, with several good individual performances but, overall, still too much that was loose.
Off-spinner Robert Croft had a rare bad day, Houghton twice in an over launching him for six.
